chunks: Three narrators - Muhammad bin Hammam - from Ahmad bin Mabindath - from Ahmad bin Hilal - from Umayya bin Ali al-Qayssi who said: I said to Abu Ja'far Muhammad bin Ali al-Rida (peace be upon him): Who is the successor after you?

He said: My son Ali and Ali's two sons. Then he pondered for a while, then raised his head and said: Confusion will occur then. I said: If that occurs, where will we go? He kept silent and then said: Nowhere - until he said it three times. I repeated my question to him, so he said: To Medina. I said: Which of the two Medinas? He said: This Medina of ours. Is there another one besides it?
ai.seo_question: Who is the successor of Imam al-Rida and where will the guidance continue after the period of confusion?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the transition from the era of the Twelve Imams to the Great Occultation, where Imam al-Rida (AS) foretells a period of 'hirah' (confusion) regarding the successor's location. By specifying 'our Medina' rather than just the geographical city, he emphasizes the spiritual and dynastic centrality of the Ahl al-Bayt, distinguishing the true seat of authority from mere political capitals. This narrative serves as a foundational text for understanding the Shi'a concept of the Imam's hidden presence and the eventual return to the spiritual heart of the faith.
